summary: Acute pulmonary infection acquired outside the healthcare setting; a leading infectious cause of hospitalization and death in older and comorbid adults. Presents with cough, fever, dyspnea, pleuritic pain, and a new infiltrate on imaging. Site-of-care and severity are set by PSI (preferred over CURB-65, 2019 ATS/IDSA, strong) or the 9-criteria minor/2-criteria major severe-CAP definition; the 2019 guideline retired HCAP as a category. Empiric antibacterials are chosen by site of care and comorbidities, with culture-guided de-escalation at 48 hours.

guidelines.name: 2025 ATS update — ATS only, IDSA is NOT a co-sponsor; answers 4 questions only, everything else still follows 2019

news.what: Peer-reviewed dissent, "We Dissent: Lessons From the 2025 Community-Acquired Pneumonia Guidelines," Clin Infect Dis 2026;82(4):625 — the 2025 ATS changes are contested, not settled; specific objections not reviewed for this card.

2025 ATS update (ATS only, IDSA not a co-sponsor) makes four changes to the 2019 baseline: lung ultrasound conditionally acceptable alt to CXR; against empiric antibacterials in outpatients without comorbidities who are virus-positive (conditional); duration for outpatients/non-severe inpatients reaching early stability shortened to <5 days, minimum 3 (conditional), vs. severe CAP 5+ days (strong); corticosteroids against in non-severe hospitalized CAP (strong), for in severe hospitalized CAP (conditional, low-quality evidence).
ATS press release announcing the steroid and duration recommendations from the 2025 update.
CDC's 2025 antibiotic stewardship update names CAP explicitly as a stewardship target condition.

review.checked: 31 claims · 13 searches · both fluoroquinolone label PDFs parsed directly

blocking.claim: Ceftaroline (Teflaro) listed as an anti-MRSA cephalosporin
blocking.says: Its CABP indication covers Staphylococcus aureus METHICILLIN-SUSCEPTIBLE ISOLATES ONLY. Only the skin-infection indication includes MRSA. On a CAP card from which vancomycin and linezolid were cut, this is the only row a provider scanning for MRSA coverage can land on, and it is the wrong answer.

blocking.claim: The rendered card silently omits vancomycin and linezolid
blocking.says: The renderer normalises cards against a fixed key whitelist. 'cutForSpace' is not in it and is dropped, and the three cut agents live only there. In the shipped card a provider sees eight agents, none covering MRSA, with no indication that vancomycin or linezolid exist. The 8-row cap was the wrong thing to protect: a formatting limit should never outrank coverage completeness.

fixes.claim: Gaps section says the fluoroquinolone wording was never directly parsed
fixes.change: DELETE — the gap is closed. Both PDFs retrieved and extracted; all four boxed-warning elements present and the card's wording is accurate. The declared weak point was clean.
The cited label is tablets for oral use and its Recent Major Changes record the injection form being removed. Cite an injection label alongside it.

fixes.claim: 'Treat the four 2025 changes as contested, not settled'
fixes.change: Overstates the dissent. It PRAISES the shortened durations and objects specifically to the virus-positive antibacterial recommendation and the guideline process.

fixes.claim: Severe-CAP criterion counts given without the decision rule
fixes.change: Add the threshold: one major OR three or more of nine minor. Severity gates two of the four recommendations the card asserts, so without it a provider cannot apply the card's own guidance.
